UpSet plot of feature sets with horizontally aligned enrichment terms

Source: R/plot_upset_h.R
plot_upset_h.Rd

Combines an UpSet plot with row annotations for intersection size and optional textboxes of top enriched functional terms.

Usage

plot_upset_h(
  set_list,
  enrich_list = NULL,
  enrich_category = NULL,
  enrich_top_n = 3,
  enrich_rank_by = "p.adjust",
  enrich_threshold = 0.05,
  enrich_wrap_width = NULL,
  set_order = NULL,
  intersection_order = NULL,
  intersection_labels = NULL,
  intersection_colours = NULL,
  fontsize = 8,
  ...
)

Arguments

set_list

A named list of character vectors of feature sets (e.g., list(Exp1_Up = ..., Exp1_Down = ..., Exp2_Up = ..., Exp2_Down = ...)). Empty input sets and zero-size intersections are excluded from the plot.

enrich_list

A named enrichment list for intersections, such as the output of enrichGO_list()$all or enrichR_list(). Each named element should be a data.frame with Cluster, Description, and the column named by enrich_rank_by. If NULL (default), no enrichment terms are displayed. The Cluster column may contain binary combination names or displayed UpSet labels. Displayed labels are auto-generated from names(set_list) by joining participating set names with _, and may be overridden with intersection_labels. See plot_modules_h() for the same per-category enrichment parameter convention. When enrich_category is a vector, each category is shown as a separate column in the annotation textbox.

enrich_category

Category name(s) of enrichment to display: a single string (e.g. "BP"), or a vector for multiple categories (e.g. c("BP", "CC")). Categories must be present in enrich_list.

enrich_top_n

Top N enrichment terms per intersection. A single integer (default: 3) is recycled for all categories in enrich_category. Supply an integer vector of matching length for per-category control.

enrich_rank_by

Numeric column used to rank enrichment terms within each intersection. A single string (default: "p.adjust") is recycled for all categories in enrich_category. Supply a character vector of matching length for per-category control. Also used for colour-coding: terms with values below enrich_threshold are shown in black, terms above in grey.

enrich_threshold

Threshold for colour-coding enrichment terms (default: 0.05). Terms where enrich_rank_by column value falls below this threshold are drawn in black, terms above in grey. Supply a vector matching enrich_category for per-category control, or set to NULL to skip colour-coding (all terms black).

enrich_wrap_width

Optional maximum enrichment term width in cm. The default NULL disables wrapping.

set_order

Optional order of the sets. When NULL (default), sets are ordered by decreasing size. Pass a character vector of set names to control display order.

intersection_order

Optional order of intersection rows. When NULL (default), intersections are ordered by decreasing combination size. Pass a character vector of combination names (as returned by ComplexHeatmap::comb_name()), or a numeric permutation of their indices, to specify a custom order.

intersection_labels

Optional named character vector mapping comb_name binary patterns to custom intersection names, overriding the auto-generated defaults. E.g., c("1010" = "Concordant_Up", "0101" = "Concordant_Down"). Entries for patterns not present in the combination matrix cause an error.

intersection_colours

Optional named colour vector for intersections. Names must match the binary combination patterns used by intersection_labels (e.g. "1010"). Colours are used for the intersection bars and combination marks.

fontsize

Base font size (default: 8).

...

Additional arguments passed to ComplexHeatmap::UpSet().

Value

A ComplexHeatmap UpSet plot, with optional enrichment term annotations.

Details

The binary combination pattern and displayed intersection label are printed when the function is called. These mappings can be used as keys for intersection_labels and intersection_colours.

Examples

# Mock feature sets with reproducible intersections
genes <- paste0("G", 1:200)
set_list <- list(Exp1_Up = genes[1:60], Exp1_Down = genes[61:100],
    Exp2_Up = genes[c(1:40, 101:115)], Exp2_Down = genes[c(61:80, 116:130)])
enrich_list <- list(BP = data.frame(
    Cluster = c("Exp1_Up_Exp2_Up", "Exp1_Down_Exp2_Down"),
    Description = c("term A", "term B"), p.adjust = c(0.001, 0.04)))
intersection_colours <- c("1010" = "#0072B5", "0101" = "#D55E00")
plot_upset_h(set_list, enrich_list = enrich_list,
    enrich_category = "BP", intersection_colours = intersection_colours)
#> Intersection pattern to label mapping:
#>   1010: Exp1_Up_Exp2_Up
#>   0101: Exp1_Down_Exp2_Down
#>   1000: Exp1_Up
#>   0100: Exp1_Down
#>   0010: Exp2_Up
#>   0001: Exp2_Down

# Custom intersection order uses the binary combination patterns.
plot_upset_h(set_list,
    intersection_order = c("1010", "1000", "0101", "0100", "0010", "0001"))
#> Intersection pattern to label mapping:
#>   1010: Exp1_Up_Exp2_Up
#>   0101: Exp1_Down_Exp2_Down
#>   1000: Exp1_Up
#>   0100: Exp1_Down
#>   0010: Exp2_Up
#>   0001: Exp2_Down
